A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiffBreak, with matching authors, central methods, theorem, datasets and retained experiments. All 27 pages of v2 and 36 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: v2 reports original adversarial-attack experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, including DiffGrad and LF results, majority-vote evaluations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original attack experiments and adds protocol-specific comparisons, gradient diagnostics, sampling ablations and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: v3 omits the corrected-adjoint procedure and time-offset fix presented in v2 Section 3.2. The principal DiffGrad checkpointing procedure, guidance-gradient computation and LF optimization remain substantively unchanged, including Algorithms 1–3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate adversarial image classification on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet under single-purification and majority-vote defenses. The additional evaluations vary procedures and sampling counts within this retained coverage; the resubmission discussion introduces no separately evaluated application dataset.

E2.justification: v3 adds direct DiffHammer-with-DiffGrad comparisons, extends DiffAttack-with-DiffGrad comparisons to GDMP, and evaluates BPDA and Surrogate under majority voting. The Adjoint-DiffGrad comparisons from v2 Tables 1–2 disappear. These substantially change comparator membership within the reported experiments.

E3.justification: v2 principally reports 100-iteration attacks with 128/16 EOT samples for CIFAR-10/ImageNet. v3 separates 10-iteration one-shot evaluation, a 20-iteration protocol testing 20 final replicas, and 100-iteration comparisons testing multiple copies at each step. EOT and evaluation counts vary explicitly by protocol, with additional sampling ablations.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's DiffAttack analysis and qualitative examples, v3 adds controlled diagnostics for EOT sampling, time inconsistency, omitted guidance gradients and incorrect surrogate gradients (Figure 2), plus a CuDNN discrepancy check. Appendix I adds a tabulated evaluation-copy ablation using 1, 10 and 128 copies.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix D.2 newly reports 20 repetitions per EOT-gradient sampling condition and means over 10 repetitions for surrogate-gradient diagnostics. These localized statistical additions do not establish repeated full-benchmark evaluations. Formal confidence intervals and error bars remain absent, now explicitly acknowledged in Appendix A.

E6.justification: Results are substantially supplemented or replaced across the separated protocols. For WRN-28-10/DiffPure, v2 reports 8.59% SP accuracy, while v3 reports 48.05% under 10-step one-shot evaluation and 30.86% under the final-20-copy protocol; differing conditions prevent a direct performance comparison. New diagnostic and runtime results appear, while LF results remain unchanged between v2 Table 4 and v3 Table 3.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1, its proof, and the diffusion and guidance-gradient derivations are retained. v3 adds formal robustness definitions in Section 3.3 and a gradient-dispersion definition with a convergence argument in Appendix D.2. There is no new central theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction now identify flawed stochastic evaluation as a second central explanation for inflated robustness, alongside incorrect gradients. v3 claims a statistically grounded majority-vote protocol as a contribution and foregrounds the ineffectiveness of prior attack enhancements. The central DBP vulnerability and LF attack claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning resubmission risk and the distinctions between worst-case, average-path and majority-vote robustness. It explicitly separates empirical defenses from certified variants and adds limitations concerning LF adversarial training and statistical reporting. It also qualifies when stochastic noise must be reproduced for correct gradients.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents deterministic CuDNN execution, parallel EOT processing with separate reproducible paths, correct-surrogate support, and detailed A100 latency and throughput information. The core pseudocode, LF hyperparameters, purification settings and DiffBreak code-access information are largely retained.

R1.justification: The positioning relative to DiffHammer changes substantially: v2 describes its continuous-time gradients as accurate, whereas v3 characterizes them as flawed surrogate gradients while crediting its evaluation-protocol critique. Majority voting is repositioned as a proposed statistical protocol. Lucas et al. is added, while Yeh et al. is removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. A dedicated evaluation-protocol section is introduced, LF moves into Section 5, countermeasures are grouped in Section 6, and the impact statement moves into an expanded appendix. Existing appendix material is substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column layout with extensive reflow and text wrapping around tables. Tables are reorganized to distinguish evaluation protocols, and a new four-panel diagnostic figure is added. The original method diagram and qualitative examples are retained, resized or relocated, and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Separating evaluation protocols and adding gradient diagnostics, sampling ablations and runtime measurements improves evidential support and transparency over v2. The gains are tempered by overinterpretation of some new evidence: Appendix D.2 treats 100% relative gradient error as establishing near-orthogonality, which that metric alone cannot show. The central theorem and LF results remain unchanged.
